{'index': 0, 'translation': "Apple may launch its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses as early as next year. They will integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri into the real world. Here's what we expect."}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'Core Features'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'First of all, these glasses are AI glasses, not AR glasses. That means they will primarily be operated by voice and camera, as they will not come with any display.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': "The camera will let Siri observe the real-world environment around you, answer questions, provide information, and translate signs. Another feature we're very likely to see is the ability to ask Siri to save an image of something and then remind you about it later — this feature first appeared in leaks of macOS 26.7."}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'They will also have built-in speakers for playing music and other audio, so you can use them like open-ear headphones.'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': "On the other hand, however, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the glasses may not be able to take photos and videos properly. Meta's Ray-Ban glasses recently sparked major privacy controversies, and Apple may want to avoid repeating the same mistakes."}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'Design and Styles'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'Unlike Meta, Apple is not partnering with an existing eyewear manufacturer to design these glasses. According to Bloomberg, the company is designing them itself and is developing several different styles:'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': 'Large rectangular frames reminiscent of the Ray-Ban Wayfarer style; a smaller rectangular design similar to those worn by Apple CEO Tim Cook; larger oval or round frames; and smaller, more refined oval or round styles.'}

{'index': 9, 'translation': 'The frames are reportedly made of acetate, a material that is more durable and premium than plastic. Apple will also offer several colour options, including black, ocean blue, and light brown.'}

{'index': 10, 'translation': 'Health Features'}

{'index': 11, 'translation': 'Apple is reportedly considering positioning this product as a health device in future product iterations. That means it could include a heart rate monitor (similar to the AirPods Pro 3), as well as other software features (such as Workout Buddy from the Apple Watch), to make it more useful.'}

{'index': 12, 'translation': "Beyond that, how Apple will make these glasses more useful for health remains unclear — but don't expect these features in the first generation."}

{'index': 13, 'translation': 'Release Date'}

{'index': 14, 'translation': "Zach Chadwick's Top Comments"}

{'index': 15, 'translation': "Like the Apple Vision Pro, this is a niche product. Unless they're sunglasses or prescription glasses, most people don't walk around with glasses on their face. People are more comfortable with the device already in their hands. Another thing collecting dust on a table at your local Apple Store."}

{'index': 16, 'translation': "Spatial computing won't be the next mainstream thing for the masses. People still want what they've always wanted: a powerful device that fits in their pocket and has battery life that lasts a day or more. Let them connect and play immersive games with desktop-quality graphics."}

{'index': 17, 'translation': 'Or let them play a game of solitaire.'}

{'index': 18, 'translation': "It's really not that hard. 🤷🏽\u200d♂️"}

{'index': 19, 'translation': 'Recent reports suggest Apple will unveil these glasses at WWDC 2027, giving developers time to prepare. They will then go on sale later that same year. The most likely launch is in September, alongside the 20th-anniversary all-glass iPhone. You can learn more here.'}

{'index': 20, 'translation': "Are you looking forward to Apple's first smart glasses? Leave a comment and let us know."}
